title: Frozen Model-Visible Representation Taxonomy for Biological Foundation-Model Routes
classification_unit: one grounded input route: a source object plus its transformation chain to the model-visible form consumed by the model
organizing_principle: Partition routes by the model-visible carrier mechanism. Biological modality, lifecycle phase, text role, and fusion topology are orthogonal dimensions; they should not be used as top-level categories unless they change the carrier class seen by the model.

families.name: Text-native token streams
families.definition: Routes whose visible carrier is ordinary text tokens: plain prompts, questions, instructions, and text scaffolds. The source may be biological, but the model sees language tokens rather than a biological serialization or dense embedding.
families.structural_criterion: The generative backbone receives standard text tokens as the visible carrier.

leaves.name: Plain language prompts and questions
leaves.definition: Natural-language prompts, questions, or conversational turns that reach the model as ordinary text without a biological serialization layer.
include_when: The visible carrier is a plain question, instruction, or conversational turn.
No specialized biological serializer is required before model intake.
exclude_when: The prompt is primarily a slot-filled biological template or metadata schema.
The route is a serialized cell, gene, or ranked biological sentence.
The visible carrier is a dense embedding, image, or diffusion state.

leaves.name: Structured biological prompts and metadata templates
leaves.definition: Text prompts that encode explicit biological slots, metadata fields, task definitions, or benchmark scaffolds while still remaining ordinary text tokens.
include_when: The text contains explicit biological fields or templated slots.
The prompt carries structured context such as gene, chromosome, indication, perturbation, interaction, or variant identifiers.
exclude_when: The input is only a plain conversational question.
The route is a serialized cell sentence, gene list, or ranked profile.
The visible carrier is a learned embedding or an image.

families.name: Serialized biological text
families.definition: Routes where biological objects are rendered into text strings that preserve domain structure, such as cell sentences, gene sentences, ranked profiles, or serialized neighborhood context.
families.structural_criterion: The model-visible form is a text serialization of biological content rather than ordinary prose prompt text.

leaves.name: Serialized cell, gene, or spatial sentences
leaves.definition: Cell-level, neighborhood-level, or gene-centric biological content serialized into sentence-like text before model intake.
include_when: Source objects are converted into cell sentences, spatial sentences, or gene sentences.
The visible carrier is a textual summary of biological context across one or more cells or neighborhoods.
exclude_when: The route is plain prompt text without biological serialization.
The visible carrier is a learned embedding prefix or a raster image.

leaves.name: Ranked or quantitative profile serializations
leaves.definition: Textual routes whose visible form is a ranked, ordered, or quantitative biological profile rendered as text, including expression hierarchies and perturbation-style delta sentences.
include_when: The route is expressed as ranked gene lists, ordered expression hierarchies, or text-based quantitative profile prompts.
The textual form is directly tied to expression, perturbation, or response ordering.
exclude_when: The route is an embedding prefix or image patch representation.
The route is a generic prose prompt with no biological serialization.

families.name: Learned continuous carriers
families.definition: Routes whose visible carrier is a learned dense vector, prefix block, query-token block, adapter-mediated embedding, or pooled latent representation inserted into the backbone.
families.structural_criterion: The source is converted into continuous embeddings, soft tokens, or learned latent blocks before reaching the generator.

leaves.name: Direct projected embeddings
leaves.definition: A continuous embedding projected from a biological encoder into the language or multimodal backbone, typically through a linear layer or latent-space projector.
include_when: The route explicitly projects biological inputs into an embedding space or unified latent space.
The visible carrier is a dense vector block rather than text tokens or image patches.
exclude_when: The carrier is a fixed prefix or soft-prompt block rather than direct projection.
The carrier is an image patch sequence or a discrete biological token stream.
The carrier is a diffusion state or a coordinate constraint.

leaves.name: Connector-mediated or prefix-carried embeddings
leaves.definition: A dense carrier that reaches the backbone through a learned connector such as cross-attention, a resampler, a query-former, an adapter, or a fixed prefix-style token block.
include_when: The route explicitly uses cross-attention, a resampler, a query-former, an adapter, or a learned prefix block.
The biological content is converted to dense tokens before fusion with the backbone.
exclude_when: The route is a fixed image raster or a discrete biological token stream.
The route is a direct projection without a mediator.
The route is a diffusion state or a coordinate/backbone carrier.

leaves.name: Pooled or aggregated embeddings
leaves.definition: A continuous carrier formed by aggregating multiple inputs into one embedding before model intake, such as averaging selected-cell embeddings or similar pooling operations.
include_when: The route compresses multiple biological items into one embedding before downstream use.
The visible form is a pooled representation rather than a single-source projection.
exclude_when: The route keeps separate tokens for each instance in the prompt.
The route uses raw images, discrete tokens, or a diffusion state.

families.name: Visual raster carriers
families.definition: Routes whose visible carrier is a raster image, image patch, slide tile, or other visual tensor processed by a vision encoder or equivalent visual front end.
families.structural_criterion: The source is presented as pixels, patches, or visual tokens rather than language tokens or dense embeddings alone.

leaves.name: Raw biomedical image inputs
leaves.definition: Histology, microscopy, pathology, or rendered biomedical image inputs presented directly as raster images or patch tensors.
include_when: The route starts from a raw image patch or whole-slide image.
The visible carrier is an image tensor or patch grid.
exclude_when: The route is a projected embedding or text prompt.
The route is a diffusion state or a discrete biological token stream.

leaves.name: Patch-context or case-level visual reasoning
leaves.definition: A visual route where multiple patches or registered sections are combined into a case-level image context before prediction or reasoning.
include_when: The route uses neighboring patches, serial sections, or case-level visual context.
The visible carrier is still visual, but the unit is a patch set or contextualized slide view.
exclude_when: The route uses only a single raw patch without contextual aggregation.
The route is text-only or embedding-only.

leaves.name: Rendered sequence or document images
leaves.definition: Biological sequences or document-like inputs rendered as images before model intake, including OCR-style sequence images.
include_when: The route renders DNA, sequence, or document content as an image before model intake.
The visible carrier is a rasterized document or sequence image rather than token text.
exclude_when: The route is a plain text prompt or a direct embedding.
The route is a biological token stream.

families.name: Discrete biological symbol streams
families.definition: Routes whose biological source is represented as a discrete token stream native to, or added to, the tokenizer rather than as prose text or a dense embedding.
families.structural_criterion: The model-visible carrier is a tokenized biological sequence or structured biological symbol stream.

leaves.name: Tokenized biological corpus streams
leaves.definition: Biological sequence corpora tokenized into model-visible tokens, typically with an extended tokenizer or chunking protocol.
include_when: The route uses tokenized DNA, RNA, protein, or related sequence corpora.
The visible form is a chunked biological token stream rather than a prompt or embedding.
exclude_when: The route is an ordinary text prompt or instruction.
The route is a dense embedding prefix or image patch input.

leaves.name: Multi-track structural token streams
leaves.definition: A token stream that explicitly preserves multiple structural tracks or aligned symbol alphabets, such as sequence plus secondary-structure or tertiary-structure tracks.
include_when: The route preserves several aligned structural tracks in one discrete token stream.
The visible carrier is a structured symbolic alphabet, not an embedding.
exclude_when: The route is a single-track tokenized corpus.
The route is a continuous prefix, image patch, or diffusion state.

leaves.name: Atomic gene symbol tokens
leaves.definition: Routes where gene symbols or similar canonical biological tokens are treated as atomic vocabulary items rather than subword fragments.
include_when: The tokenizer vocabulary is explicitly augmented with biological symbols.
Gene names are treated as atomic tokens during instruction tuning or prompt assembly.
exclude_when: The route uses generic prompt text without vocabulary augmentation.
The route is a continuous embedding prefix or a discrete sequence corpus.

families.name: Geometric and diffusion-state carriers
families.definition: Routes whose visible form is a geometric constraint, coordinate state, or noisy latent state used by a diffusion or structure-generation model.
families.structural_criterion: The model-visible carrier is a coordinate, constraint, or time-indexed noisy latent state rather than a token sequence or patch grid.

leaves.name: Noisy diffusion states
leaves.definition: A time-indexed noisy latent state or training state used directly in a diffusion process.
include_when: The route exposes noisy coordinates or another diffusion-time latent state to the model.
The carrier is part of forward or reverse diffusion dynamics.
exclude_when: The route is a static coordinate constraint or a text prompt.
The route is an image, token stream, or dense embedding prefix.

leaves.name: Coordinate or backbone conditioning
leaves.definition: A geometric conditioning route in which the model receives coordinates, backbones, substructures, or point-cloud-derived geometry as the visible carrier.
include_when: The route conditions on backbone coordinates, substructures, or point clouds.
The model-visible form is geometric rather than textual.
exclude_when: The route is an abstract symbolic label or a free-text prompt.
The route is a noisy diffusion state rather than a stable geometric condition.

leaves.name: Symbolic structural constraints
leaves.definition: A non-textual or lightly symbolic structural condition such as symmetry, topology class, or other geometry-level control signals supplied to the generator.
include_when: The route conditions generation with symbolic structural labels or abstract geometry constraints.
The carrier is a constraint signal rather than a language prompt or a dense embedding.
exclude_when: The route is a free-form natural-language caption or question.
The route is a coordinate/backbone carrier or a noisy diffusion state.

orthogonal_dimensions.name: Biological modality
orthogonal_dimensions.definition: The underlying source domain of the route, treated separately from the carrier mechanism because the same modality can be serialized, embedded, rasterized, or diffused.

orthogonal_dimensions.name: Lifecycle phase
orthogonal_dimensions.definition: The training or evaluation stage at which the route is used. This prevents training-only targets, generated outputs, baselines, and inference inputs from being conflated.

orthogonal_dimensions.name: Text role / route status
orthogonal_dimensions.definition: The role played by text or symbolic material in the route, including whether it is an actual model input, a paired training input, a target, or a baseline or auxiliary prompt.

orthogonal_dimensions.name: Fusion topology
orthogonal_dimensions.definition: How the carrier is inserted into or combined with the generative backbone. This is orthogonal to the carrier type itself.

orthogonal_dimensions.name: Source-to-carrier transformation
orthogonal_dimensions.definition: The dominant transformation applied to the source object before it becomes model-visible. This captures whether the route is serialized, tokenized, projected, rasterized, aggregated, or driven by diffusion.

category_errors_prevented: Collapsing prompt text, serialized biological text, and learned continuous carriers into one bucket.
Treating image rasters and projected image features as the same mechanism.
Treating tokenized biological corpora as ordinary prose.
Using source modality alone as the top-level axis when the visible carrier mechanism is the relevant structural criterion.
Folding diffusion-time noisy states into static coordinates or embeddings.
Folding training-only targets, generated outputs, baselines, and ablations into the same class as actual model inputs.
unresolved_questions: Whether future corpora should split graph-derived textual reasoning from other structured biological prompts once graph structure becomes a first-class visible carrier.
Whether pooled multi-cell embeddings should remain a small dedicated leaf or be merged into the broader connector-mediated embedding leaf if more aggregation-heavy routes appear.
Whether rendered sequence-image routes should stay under visual raster carriers or be split into a separate document and OCR-style leaf if that interface becomes common.
